key_insight: Sequence-to-sequence, attention-based deep models (transformer-style) consistently outperform fully connected and simpler architectures at mapping noisy measured quantum output distributions to distributions closer to the ideal (noise-mitigated) outputs.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of mitigating noise in output probability distributions from measured quantum circuits—improving the fidelity of classical estimates derived from noisy quantum hardware without requiring changes to the quantum device or full error correction.
method: Benchmarked multiple neural architectures (fully connected, convolutional, recurrent, and transformer/seq2seq attention models) on datasets of noisy vs. ideal output distributions.
Evaluated different design and training modalities to identify which architectures generalize best for distribution-to-distribution correction.
Selected and validated sequence-to-sequence, attention-based models as the most effective approach for producing noise-mitigated output probability distributions.
impact: Provides a practical, software-level pathway for AI/ML practitioners and quantum researchers to reduce measurement noise in near-term quantum experiments, enabling more reliable downstream hybrid ML workflows and empirical studies on NISQ devices.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing mitigation quality (e.g., total variation distance or KL divergence) across architectures (FC, CNN, RNN, Transformer).
Schematic pipeline: noisy quantum circuit → measured distribution → seq2seq attention model → mitigated distribution → comparison with ideal.
Attention map example showing learned alignment between noisy input sequence bins and corrected output probabilities.
Before/after distribution plots (stacked probability histograms) illustrating reduction in error for representative circuits.
paper_title: Deep Learning Approaches to Quantum Error Mitigation
paper_authors: Leonardo Placidi, Ifan Williams, Enrico Rinaldi, Daniel Mills, Cristina Cîrstoiu
